bridge.title: Star
bridge.content: Formerly known as SubDAOs, Stars are smaller, specialized, decentralized ecosystems that exist within the broader Sky Ecosystem and are tied to the Sky Protocol. Their core design enables a derisked, second layer of the ecosystem to foster fast-moving, risk-adjusted innovation, growth and experimentation. Stars also enable delegation of responsibility and risk within specific, highly complex areas. In general, complexity, responsibility, decision-making authority and risk is off-loaded from Sky Core and pushed to the Stars, except if the Sky Atlas specifies otherwise.

bridge.title: Star Scope Bounded Mutable Alignment Artifacts
bridge.content: Star Scope Alignment Artifacts are internal Scope Alignment Artifacts for Stars. All Stars begin with a standard genesis Scope Artifact that they can modify. They can also create additional Scope Artifacts with new Scopes. Unlike Sky, Star Scope Artifacts have much fewer restrictions on how they can be modified and what strategic opportunities they can cover.

bridge.title: Sealing
bridge.content: Sealing is a form of governance participation unlocked by SKY and MKR. When a user Seals their SKY or MKR tokens, they immediately begin to earn significant rewards. They must pay an Exit Fee to access their governance tokens again. This mechanism makes it more beneficial to Seal if the user anticipates remaining in the system long-term. Because there's a penalty for exiting, Sealing helps generate additional skin in the game and increases long-term alignment among ecosystem participants.

bridge.title: Activation
bridge.content: Activation is a less committed version of Sealing. When a user Activates their SKY tokens, they receive Activation Rewards, but don't have to Seal their tokens behind an Exit Fee. The Activated SKY can be freely Deactivated at any time.

bridge.title: Season System
bridge.content: Delegate Contracts operate on a Season system that starts on the Monday of the 11th full week of the first quarter of the year, and ends on the Friday of the 12th full week of the first quarter of the following year.

bridge.title: Lifetime
bridge.content: Delegate Contracts are considered Seasonally Active from the moment they are created until the end of the Season in which they were created. Delegate Contracts expire and lose their voting power at the end of the second Season following their creation, giving them a total lifetime of up to approximately two (2) years and two (2) weeks.

bridge.title: AD Buffer And Loss Of Budget Stream
bridge.content: If an AD loses a part of its budget stream due to a transition from Prime Delegate (PD) to Aligned Delegate (AD), their AD Buffer will stay paying out its excess funds until the remaining balance equals one month's budget allocation. If an AD loses its entire budget stream, the full contents of the AD Buffer can be spent.

bridge.title: Core Facilitators
bridge.content: If a Facilitator has responsibility for Sky Core's Support Scope or the Stability Scope, they are designated "Core Facilitators". Core Facilitators can only provide services to Sky Core and cannot be assigned responsibility for Star Scopes.

bridge.title: Stars Scope Assignment
bridge.content: Stars can assign responsibility of their Scopes to Facilitators. Being assigned responsibility of a Star Scope requires the Facilitator to assume full responsibility for all aspects of that Scope. A Facilitator cannot accept partial responsibility or selectively manage certain elements of a Scope.

bridge.title: Eligibility For Star Scopes
bridge.content: If a Facilitator does not have responsibility for Sky Core's Support Scope or Stability Scope, they can be assigned responsibility for Star Scopes.

bridge.title: Required Notice To Exit
bridge.content: Once a Facilitator has agreed to take responsibility for a Star Scope, they must provide a minimum of three (3) months' notice before relinquishing their duties. This rule can be waived where the Facilitator can demonstrate a clear breach of good faith or other event of misalignment justifying the expedited exit.

bridge.title: Role Of Support And Governance Facilitators
bridge.content: The Support or Governance Facilitators are responsible for coordinating emergency-situation processes to ensure they are civil, consistently applied and aligned.The Governance Facilitators are responsible for publishing Polls and confirming Poll outcomes; and identifying whether the community or external actors have attempted to abuse or game the emergency voting system.

bridge.title: Declaring An Emergency
bridge.content: The ability to formally declare an emergency will be reserved for the Facilitators due to their proximity to, and knowledge of, the Sky Protocol and surrounding ecosystem. Any participant in the Sky Ecosystem, including Ecosystem Actors, Aligned Delegates or other community members, can request a Scope Facilitator to declare an emergency. The Facilitators are granted broad discretion in handling such requests.

bridge.title: Emergency Response Process
bridge.content: The Emergency Response Process is defined in the subdocuments herein.

bridge.title: Unknown Or Contentious Remedies
bridge.content: If a remedy is not known or is contentious, the Support or Governance Facilitators shall coordinate an emergency governance call to discuss solutions and a plan for subsequent actions. The Facilitators should invite known stakeholders to the call, where appropriate.

bridge.title: Spark Pre-launch Token Rewards
bridge.content: Spark has a pre-launch token rewards program based on the usage of its lending platform. Users of the platform will receive an airdrop of SPK tokens, depending on how much and how long they have used the platform during the pre-launch token reward period. These rewards are only for users on Ethereum Mainnet. There are two phases to the Spark pre-launch token rewards: Phase 1 and Phase 2.Phase 1 of pre-launch token rewards was active from August 20 2023 and lasted for nine months, ending on May 20 2024. 60m SPK tokens were allocated in this period.Phase 2 of pre-launch token rewards began at the completion of the first phase on May 20 2024, and lasts until the issuance of the SPK token. 6.66m SPK tokens per month will be allocated during this second phase, calculated on a per-block basis according to the formula below.The SPK rewards formula, designed to counter cheating, is as follows:Airdrop = 80% \* (Dai Borrows - sDAI Supplies \* sDAI Liquidation Threshold) + 20% \* (ETH Supplies - ETH Borrows / ETH Liquidation Threshold)

bridge.title: Special Pre-launch Token Reward Programs
bridge.content: The Support Facilitators can activate a new SPK token pre-launch token reward airdrop program to capture other growth opportunities.The program can last until the moment SPK launches, or a shorter duration, which must be declared by the Support Facilitators. When activated by the Support Facilitators, the exact details of the special pre-launch token reward airdrop program must be specified in A.2.5 - Star Incubation - Star Specific Support - Special Pre-launch Token Reward Programs Details.The SPK tokens for the future Spark Airdrop are allocated between all borrowers based on a formula announced by the Support Facilitators and specified in the above cited document. bridge.title: Stablecoin Collateral Reserve
bridge.content: Sky must maintain a reserve of at least 20% of the total Dai and USDS Supply held as Cash Stablecoins, or assets and exposure that can rapidly be converted to Cash Stablecoins.

bridge.title: Cash Stablecoin Definition And List
bridge.content: A Cash Stablecoin is defined as either a Stablecoin listed in A.3.4 - Collateral Portfolio - List Of Cash Stablecoin; a technically secure DeFi token that can be instantly converted to a listed Stablecoin; or a custody solution that can be converted into a listed Stablecoin within 30 minutes. The Stability Facilitators can modify the above cited document through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle to react to changing market conditions, opportunities or risks. The modification of the list can include adding or removing Cash Stablecoins, or changing the terms of existing Cash Stablecoins on the list.

List of Cash Stablecoins:

bridge.title: Cash Stablecoin Peg Stability Module Upgrades
bridge.content: The mechanism for holding and making Cash Stablecoins available to support the liquidity of Dai and USDS can be upgraded to a superior technical, financial or legal solution by a proposal from the Stability Facilitators through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle.The Stability Facilitators may specify requirements for how Star Advisory teams deploy USDS generated from their Star Vault.

bridge.title: Asset Liability Management
bridge.content: To ensure adequate liquidity, Cash Stablecoins are managed through a simple Asset Liability Management framework. This framework allocates excess Cash Stablecoins into low-risk RWA assets, and draws on these assets to replenish the Cash Stablecoins when they fall too low.

bridge.title: Excess Cash Stablecoins
bridge.content: If the Dai and USDS Collateral portfolio contains more than 30% of Cash Stablecoins as defined above, then any Cash Stablecoins above the 30% mark must be allocated towards the collateral defined in A.3.4 - Collateral Portfolio - Asset Liability Management - Low Risk RWA.

bridge.title: Lack Of Cash Stablecoins
bridge.content: If the Dai and USDS Collateral portfolio contains less than 20% Cash Stablecoins, the assets defined in A.3.4 - Collateral Portfolio - Asset Liability Management - Low Risk RWA must be sold off to return the Cash Stablecoin exposure to 25%.

bridge.title: Surplus Buffer Upper Limit
bridge.content: This Section defines the Surplus Buffer Upper Limit and key parameters of the Smart Burn Engine.

bridge.title: Parameters
bridge.content: The amount of USDS in the Surplus Buffer that causes the Smart Burn Engine to activate, and the rate at which it uses the USDS to improve SKY liquidity, are determined by two parameters defined by the following subdocuments. The Smart Burn Engine, which defines specific parameter configuration requirements of DssFlapper, and how it should be altered are also defined in the following subdocuments.

bridge.title: Upper Limit
bridge.content: The Surplus Buffer Upper Limit determines the amount of USDS necessary for the Smart Burn Engine to activate.

bridge.title: Upper Limit Amount
bridge.content: The Surplus Buffer Upper Limit is: 55 million USDS

bridge.title: SKY Accumulation
bridge.content: The Smart Burn Engine can switch between accumulating SKY/USDS liquidity and directly accumulating SKY only.The Stability Facilitators can trigger a switch from one mode of accumulation to the other, based on market factors and input from the Stability Scope Advisors.By default, the Smart Burn Engine must be switched to directly accumulating SKY only.

bridge.title: Rate Of SKY Accumulation
bridge.content: The rate of SKY Accumulation should target the approximate net surplus income rate of the Sky Protocol. The Stability Facilitators must regularly update the relevant Smart Burn Engine parameters, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors, to ensure they continuously track the net surplus income rate.Stability Facilitators should aim to slightly underestimate the net surplus income rate. This approach allows the Surplus Buffer to slowly grow above its upper limit, while ensuring that most of the net surplus income is used by the Smart Burn Engine, Activation, and Sealing.

bridge.title: SKY Maximum Price
bridge.content: If the SKY price surpasses 0.33 USD, the Smart Burn Engine must be turned off, and the Surplus Buffer Upper Limit set to infinity via an Executive Vote.

bridge.title: DssFlapper
bridge.content: DssFlapper is the current implementation of the contract which processes Smart Burn Engine transactions once activated. The DssFlapper includes the following parameters: hop, want, bump, pip and receiver. Stability Facilitators can propose DssFlapper reconfiguration within limits defined in each parameter's corresponding document. The Stability Facilitators can propose these changes directly to an Executive Vote, with the exception of the receiver and pip . These parameters always require a Governance Poll, unless the Sky Protocol is in a state of emergency, such that the expedited modification of parameters is necessary to prevent loss of funds.

bridge.title: Hop Parameter
bridge.content: Flapper.hop: Minimum seconds interval between kicks.Determines maximum allowed frequency of transactions taking place.Maximum hop must be set to equal the approximate Effective Rate of MKR Accumulation defined in A.3.5 - Surplus Buffer And Smart Burn Engine - Parameters depending on the corresponding configuration of bump parameter.

bridge.title: Hop Parameter Amount Of Seconds
bridge.content: The hop parameter is: 10,249 seconds

bridge.title: Want Parameter
bridge.content: Flapper.want: Relative multiplier of the oracle price needed for the swap.For example, 0.98 \* WAD allows for a 2% worse price than the MKR/USD reference oracle (pip) price used in the system. want must not exceed 2%.

bridge.title: Want Parameter Number
bridge.content: The want parameter is: 0.98

bridge.title: Bump Parameter
bridge.content: Vow.bump: Minimum amount of Dai above Surplus Buffer Upper Limit required for eligible market transaction. bump is the amount of Dai used to get MKR. The bump should be set to minimize both price impact and transaction costs, based on an analysis of network conditions provided by the Stability Scope Advisors and the anticipated outlook for these factors.

bridge.title: Bump Parameter Amount
bridge.content: The bump parameter is: 65,000 Dai

bridge.title: Pip Parameter
bridge.content: Flappers.pip: A reference price oracle, used for bounding the exchange rate of the swap.

bridge.title: Receiver Parameter Address

bridge.title: Parameter Reconfiguration Methodology & Frequency
bridge.content: Via the first available Executive Vote, the Stability Facilitators must update the Smart Burn Engine Dss Flapper related parameters based on cost optimization analyses provided by the Stability Scope Advisors. Due to the volatility of market impact and gas consumption, which are key factors in cost optimization, there is no fixed frequency for these updates. The Scope Advisors are responsible for continuously monitoring the Smart Burn Engine and notifying the Stability Facilitators when changes are needed. This notification must include the relevant analysis and proposed parameter adjustments within the established limits and boundaries defined by the Stability Scope.

bridge.title: Interest Rate Model Definition
bridge.content: The Interest Rate Model ("IRM") is defined by four main parameters:1. Base Rate - the starting rate at 0% utilization2. Variable Slope 1 - the rate at optimal utilization3. Variable Slope 2 - the rate at 100% utilization4. Utilization - the utilization itselfThe Base Rate, Slope 1, and Slope 2 parameters are further defined in:A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - SparkLend Risk Parameters - Base Rate Definition; A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - SparkLend Risk Parameters - Slope 1 Definition; and A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - SparkLend Risk Parameters - Slope 2 Definition.All markets except Dai use this IRM. The IRM for Dai is independent of utilization and is defined as a spread over the Core Stability Parameters Base Rate set forth in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Base Rate. The spread is determined by the Stability Facilitators, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors.

bridge.title: Cap Automators
bridge.content: Cap Automaters allow the Supply Cap defined in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - SparkLend Risk Parameters - Supply Cap Definition and the Borrow Cap defined in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - SparkLend Risk Parameters - Borrow Cap Definition to be dynamically adjusted.The Cap Automater is defined in terms of three parameters:1. gap - the target available exposure2. ttl - the cooldown period for cap increases3. max - the absolute maximum exposureAny user can permissionlessly update a covered Supply Cap or Borrow Cap so the available exposure is equal to the target, as long as the resulting exposure does not exceed the specified maximum limit and the cooldown period has elapsed in the case of increases to the Supply Cap or Borrow Cap.

bridge.title: Kill Switch
bridge.content: The kill switch disables all borrowing across SparkLend markets in the event of a depeg on key collateral assets.The kill switch is defined in terms of a threshold for specified pegged assets. If the ratio of the price of a specified asset to its peg is equal to or less than the threshold, then any user can trigger the kill switch to disable borrowing across all SparkLend markets.After the kill switch is triggered, markets can be reactivated by Sky Governance after resetting the kill switch. Resetting the kill switch is subject to the Governance Security Delay specified in A.1.9 - A2 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements.

bridge.title: SKY Launch
bridge.content: In the Endgame Token Launch Phase, SKY is launched as an upgrade to MKR. MKR can be exchanged to and from SKY at a rate of 1:24,000.

bridge.title: SKY Activation
bridge.content: SKY Activation can be done by any SKY holder through the SKY Activation Mechanism available on Ethereum Mainnet and SkyLink Deployments. SKY Activation provides USDS Rewards or Star Token Rewards.

bridge.title: Availability
bridge.content: SKY Activation will be available at the launch of the Spark Star.

bridge.title: Star Token Activation
bridge.content: Star Token Activation can be done by any Star Token holder. It is available on Ethereum Mainnet and SkyLink Destination Chains. Star Token Activation provides SKY Rewards.

bridge.title: Availability
bridge.content: Star Token Activation will be available at the launch of the Spark Star.

bridge.title: Sealing
bridge.content: Sealing is available both for SKY and MKR holders, with 1 MKR counting as 24,000 SKY. Sealing seals the principal tokens behind an Exit Fee. Sealing provides USDS Rewards or Star Token Rewards. Sealing users can also generate USDS using the USDS content of the Smart Burn Engine as collateral. Users' ability to generate USDS is based on the equivalent quantity they hold of sealed SKY. The Sealing mechanism is governed by the Stability Scope.

bridge.title: Availability
bridge.content: Sealing will be available shortly after the launch of USDS and SKY.

bridge.title: Exit Fee
bridge.content: The Sealing Exit Fee starts at 5%, and increases by 1% every six (6) months from launch, until it reaches its permanent long-term value at 15%.

bridge.title: Total Emissions
bridge.content: SKY emissions take place through two mechanisms, USDS Token Rewards and Star Token Activation.

bridge.title: USDS Rewards
bridge.content: 600 million SKY are emitted per year to be distributed through the USDS Token Reward Mechanism. Every time a new Star is launched and begins its SKY Star Token Activation Rewards, the SKY USDS Token Reward amount is reduced by an amount equivalent to the newly added rewards.

bridge.title: Star Token Activation Rewards
bridge.content: Every Star that launches, starting with Spark, will offer Star Token Activation Rewards in SKY at a rate of 80 million SKY per year. Whenever a Star launches, the SKY USDS Token Reward rate is reduced by 80m SKY per year.

bridge.title: Total Emissions
bridge.content: Every Star distributes a total of 4.9 billion Star tokens as its genesis emissions, used for Token Rewards, Contributor Bonuses, and other bootstrapping uses.

bridge.title: USDS Rewards
bridge.content: Every Star distributes a total of 2.8 billion Star tokens to USDS holders receiving Token Rewards. The rate is 700 million Star tokens per year for the first 2 years; 350 million per year from year 3-4; 175 million per year from year 5-6; and 87.5 million per year from year 7-10.

bridge.title: SKY Activation Rewards
bridge.content: Every Star distributes a total of 600 million Star tokens to Activated SKY holders. The rate is 150 million Star tokens per year for the first 2 years; 75 million per year from year 3-4; 37.5 million per year from year 5-6; and 18.75 million per year from year 7-10.

bridge.title: SKY Seal Rewards
bridge.content: Every Star distributes a total of 600 million Star tokens to Sealed SKY holders. The rate is 150 million Star tokens per year for the first 2 years; 75 million per year from year 3-4; 37.5 million per year from year 5-6; and 18.75 million per year from year 7-10.

bridge.title: Accessibility Reward
bridge.content: This Section manages the Accessibility Reward which allows Integrators to receive payment for attracting new users to the Protocol. This Section defines the signup process, marketing fee, parameters and management of the Accessibility Reward system.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: This element refers to an action by the Star, or entities acting on its behalf, that undermines trust, integrity, or fair dealing, such as deception or unethical conduct.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: The element "emergency voting system" refers to the protocol specified in A.1.14 for handling emergency and urgent situations. Confusion may potentially arise here if the reader misinterprets "emergency voting system" to apply only to situations classified as emergencies.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: The element "excess funds" refers to the amount in the AD Buffer that exceeds the required one-month budget threshold.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: A kick is an operation that is triggered periodically by the DssFlapper contract. Each operation withdraws Dai from the surplus buffer and uses that Dai to buy MKR on Uniswap v2. The MKR, along with a proportionate amount of additional Dai withdrawn from the surplus buffer, are deposited back into the Uniswap v2 liquidity pool in exchange for LP tokens. The LP tokens are then sent to the receiver address in the DssFlapper contract.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: An "oracle" is an onchain source of truth regarding some data. Most commonly in the case of Sky, a price oracle will serve as the onchain source of truth for pricing data regarding collateral or other assets. Since onchain computations must be deterministic, oracles must publish this data onchain and must be subject to cryptoeconomic guarantees to allow other actors to rely on the data they provide.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: This element clarifies that the Facilitator cannot choose to manage only certain parts of a Scope or limit their responsibility to specific tasks. They must accept the full responsibilities and manage the Scope as a whole.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: The element "potential misalignment" refers to any situation where there is a reasonable suspicion or indication that an Alignment Conserver (AC) has breached their obligations or requirements, as specified in the Atlas.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: A request to declare an emergency situation can be submitted to a Governance or Support Facilitator through a post on the Sky Forum or other communication methods specified by the Facilitators. There is no required template for submitting such a request.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: The element refers to the cumulative voting power that has been delegated to a Delegate Contract by SKY holders and Sealed Activation users.

bridge.title: Element Annotation
bridge.content: "Univ2 MKR/Dai LP Token" refers to a Liquidity Provider token in the MKR/Dai pool on Uniswap v2. Decentralized exchanges typically use liquidity pools rather than order books to minimize transaction costs. A liquidity pool contains a combination of two tokens, in this case MKR and Dai, and allows users to permissionlessly swap assets in the pool at the current market price. Liquidity Providers provide assets to the pool and in exchange receive a share of the trading fees from the pool.

bridge.title: Facilitators' Broad Discretion In Handling Requests To Declare Emergency
bridge.content:
In response to a request to declare an emergency, Facilitators may:

-   Approve the request and declare an emergency
-   Deny the request if they determine that the situation does not meet the criteria for an emergency
-   Seek additional information or clarification from the requester or other relevant parties before making a decision.Facilitators must base their decision on an informed assessment of the situation, considering the potential risks and impact on the Sky Protocol and the broader ecosystem. Facilitators should consult with domain experts such as Scope Advisors or Ecosystem Actors where appropriate.

bridge.title: Clarification of "Good Cause"
bridge.content: Research is required into what specific circumstances likely qualify as "good cause." This can include developing guidelines or a checklist of acceptable reasons that would justify delays, as well as examples of situations that would not meet this threshold.

bridge.title: Impact Of Extenuating Circumstances
bridge.content: Research should focus on the potential scope and impact of extenuating circumstances. This involves defining and analyzing possible scenarios where such circumstances can be invoked; and examining the implications for governance and accountability if such claims are overused or abused.To help control for the risk of biased decisionmaking, it would help to consider the specific criteria Facilitators should use to determine when an extenuating circumstance is considered valid. Possible research here can develop clear criteria or a decision matrix to determine the acceptability of proffered extenuating circumstances. The goal is to see if it is possible to get reasonably close to a standardized approach to assessing whether a claim of extenuating circumstances is justified.

bridge.title: Impact of misalignment on Entity's involvement with Ecosystem Actor
bridge.content: The Atlas lacks explicit logic for determining whether Entity should also be removed from its EA role or otherwise be prevented from being engaged by EAs. Entity likely did not have malign intentions in this Scenario. It is reasonable to extrapolate that, under these circumstances, derecognition from the AC role would suffice. Compare with On-call or standby role - var. 1.

bridge.title: Potential value of reputation system for Ecosystem Actors
bridge.content: This Scenario highlights the potential value of having a formal reputation system for Ecosystem Actors as well. The Resource Deals process will certainly ensure that EAs have trackable deliverables and milestones and similar accountability. But it may be wise to stand up a parallel reputation system for EAs so that questionable business practices can be made legible for the community. This is a separate but needed dimension of accountability. This is a possible Research Track.
